test_title: SSC MTS 2023 Official Paper (Held On: 11 Sept, 2023 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: In how many years will Rs. 1,60,000 become Rs. 2,79,841 at a compound interest (Compounded annually) rate of 15% per annum?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Multiplying factor for 15% compound interest annually = 1 + 15/100 = 115/100 = 23/20.

Ratio of Amount to Principal = 279841 ÷ 160000.

We know the denominator 160000 is exactly 20⁴, so we check if 279841 is 23⁴.

Since 23² = 529 and 529 × 529 = 279841, the ratio is strictly (23/20)⁴.

The exponent represents the number of compounding years.

**∴ The correct answer is 4 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal (P) = ₹1,60,000

Amount (A) = ₹2,79,841

Rate of Interest (R) = 15% per annum compounded annually

Time = n years

**Formula Used:**

A = P × (1 + R/100)ⁿ

 
• 
 
 
 Principal (P)
 ₹1,60,000
 
 
 Amount (A)
 ₹2,79,841
 
 

 Rate = 15% p.a.
 Time = n years
 
 
 
 

 
 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 279841 = 160000 × (1 + 15/100)ⁿ

⇒ 279841 ÷ 160000 = (115/100)ⁿ

⇒ 279841 ÷ 160000 = (23/20)ⁿ

⇒ Observing the denominator: 160000 = 16 × 10000 = 2⁴ × 10⁴ = 20⁴

⇒ Similarly, analyzing the numerator: 23² = 529 and 529 × 529 = 279841, therefore 279841 = 23⁴

⇒ (23/20)⁴ = (23/20)ⁿ

⇒ By comparing the bases and equating the powers, we get n = 4.

**∴ The correct answer is 4 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Half-Yearly Compounding

If the interest is compounded half-yearly instead of annually, the applied rate is halved (R/2)% and the time period becomes doubled (2n) in the CI formula.

Effective Rate of Compound Interest

For 2 years at an annual rate of R%, the effective compound interest percentage can be directly calculated using the successive percentage formula: (2R + R²/100)%.

Difference Between CI and SI

For exactly 2 years, the difference between CI and SI on the same principal is given by: CI − SI = P × (R/100)². For 3 years, the difference formula extends to: P × (R/100)² × (3 + R/100).
